sheets.rejected_alternative: A checked-in project .claude/settings.json policy: the developer controls both the repo and their home directory, so anything below the managed tier is editable and cannot deliver the guarantee.
sheets.enforcement_owner: Harness: configuration-source precedence and load-time filtering are enforced by the CLI, not by model compliance.
sheets.context_boundary: Enforcement happens at configuration and extension load before anything enters the session, so blocked skills, hooks, agents, and MCP servers never contribute a token to any context window.
sheets.lifecycle: Evaluated at every session start and at MCP or plugin load from the system-level path; applies fleet-wide until IT changes the MDM-deployed file.
sheets.failure_mode: Coverage gaps fail open: any extension type that lacks a managed allowlist knob in the installed CLI version still loads from user or repo scope, developers with local admin can edit the system file, and an older pinned CLI may predate a knob entirely; the control needs MDM file protection and CLI version pinning to actually hold.
sheets.version_caveat: Managed settings themselves are established 2025 functionality, but the fine-grained allowlist controls for hooks, plugins, marketplaces, skills, and MCP servers arrived piecemeal across later releases; I cannot name the exact setting keys or versions for each without documentation, and a dedicated allowlist for skills or agent definitions specifically may not exist at all.

sheets.primary: Managed settings composing the supply-chain locks: strictPluginOnlyCustomization true (blocks skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources), strictKnownMarketplaces plus blockedMarketplaces (only IT marketplaces), and disableSideloadFlags (rejects --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents, --mcp-config), with the IT-vetted plugins force-enabled via managed enabledPlugins and servers shipped in managed-mcp.json with allowManagedMcpServersOnly.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Distributing an IT plugin through an organization marketplace alone: it ships the sanctioned content but guarantees nothing, because developers could still load their own skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user or project sources without the managed locks.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness: managed settings sit at the top of settings precedence and cannot be overridden by any other level, so blocked sources are skipped at load time no matter what a developer writes locally or commits.
sheets.context_boundary: Enforcement happens at configuration load, before any context exists; blocked skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers are never loaded, so developer-added extension content never reaches any context window in any session.
sheets.lifecycle: Applies at every session start and on config reload on each machine for as long as IT deploys the managed policy; for each locked surface only plugin-provided and managed sources load, and the locks end only when IT removes them.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open where the lock set is incomplete: without disableSideloadFlags a developer can bypass the marketplace allowlist for a single run with CLI flags, and any laptop missing the managed deployment has no locks at all; unrecognized surface names in the array are silently ignored rather than failing.
sheets.version_caveat: disableSideloadFlags requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later; on earlier clients the sideload flags remain a bypass even with the other locks in place.

sheets.primary: Managed policy settings combining strictPluginOnlyCustomization: true (blocks skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources), force-enabled enabledPlugins from the IT marketplace, strictKnownMarketplaces plus blockedMarketplaces for source control, allowManagedHooksOnly and allowManagedMcpServersOnly as reinforcement, and disableSideloadFlags to close the CLI bypass.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Distributing an approved plugin bundle by convention: plugins alone package the sanctioned components but do nothing to stop a developer adding ~/.claude/skills or committing .claude/agents into a repo; only managed-only settings lock those surfaces.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness: all of these are managed-settings-only keys that user and project scopes cannot set, and managed settings cannot be overridden by any other level.
sheets.context_boundary: The gate operates at component discovery and load time across all sessions; blocked skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers never load, so nothing from them enters any context window.
sheets.lifecycle: Enforced at session start and on settings reload on every machine carrying the policy; marketplace blocks are checked before download so blocked sources never touch disk; lasts until IT changes the policy.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open on any machine the policy never reached, and has coverage gaps if a key is omitted: without disableSideloadFlags a developer can pass --plugin-dir, --agents, or --mcp-config for a single run; blockedMarketplaces itself fails closed since blocked sources are rejected pre-download.
sheets.version_caveat: disableSideloadFlags requires v2.1.193+; under allowManagedHooksOnly, plugin hook trust is granted by full plugin@marketplace ID, so a same-named plugin from another marketplace stays blocked; strictPluginOnlyCustomization also accepts an array to lock only selected surfaces.
